## 9. Observations from manual reading

Maintained in `OBSERVATIONS` inside scripts/audit_code.py; each entry is checked against the current text of the named line. src/ is not modified by W12; these are notes for the team.

| # | file:line | kind | observation | check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | scripts/make_holdout.py:17 | portability | `resource` is a POSIX-only module; the script cannot start on Windows. data/SOURCE.md records the holdout build under Python 3.10.12 (a non-Windows interpreter), consistent with this. | ok |
| 2 | scripts/check_data.py:20 | consistency | Reads the fixed relative path data/processed and ignores NBR_DATA_DIR / configs/common.yaml (nbr.config honours both); run from the repository root with the data copied in place. | ok |
| 3 | feat/w9-r3-cycle:src/nbr/r3_eval.py:57 | portability | Hard-coded absolute Windows path as the default gamma* source (overridable with --gamma-dir). configs/usercf.yaml (selection_source.tuning_dir) carries the same machine-specific path. | ok |
| 4 | src/nbr/usercf_eval.py:27 | style | Imports a private helper of another module (also src/nbr/usercf.py line 15 imports nbr.itemcf._topn_with_ties). The helpers are shared by design but are not part of a public interface. | ok |
| 5 | src/nbr/lr_repeat.py:101 | numerical | The tie-break popularity is recovered from the log_pop feature with expm1(log1p(pop)); the float round trip can differ from the integer pop by about 1e-12, which only matters for exact score ties. | ok |
| 6 | src/nbr/usercf.py:47 | fragility | Row/column labels are attached as ad-hoc attributes of a scipy csr_matrix; this works for the legacy csr_matrix class but would not for the newer sparse-array API (csr_array). | ok |
| 7 | src/nbr/__init__.py:1 | documentation | The package docstring lists only the W1 modules; the package now also holds repeat, baselines, explore, itemcf, combine, pipeline, features, lr_repeat, usercf and usercf_eval. | ok |
| 8 | src/nbr/pipeline.py:490 | style | Redundant inner conditional: the branch is only taken when hi is finite, so the 'inf' alternative cannot occur. Harmless. | ok |
| 9 | src/nbr/usercf_eval.py:79 | consistency | Merges every top-level key of configs/usercf.yaml into the profile config, including a second `bootstrap` block; its values equal configs/common.yaml today, so no behaviour differs. | ok |
| 10 | src/nbr/metrics.py:40 | performance | per_user_recall / per_user_ndcg / per_user_category_hit loop over users in Python (unlike the vectorised list builders); correct, but the slowest step for large eval splits. | ok |
| 11 | src/nbr/usercf_eval.py:127 | style | Library function prints progress to stdout (also line 248); nbr.pipeline reuses tune_history, so `python -m nbr tune` output interleaves these lines. | ok |

## 10. Rules used by this audit

- Files: every `*.py` under `src/nbr` and `scripts` of the worktree, plus the `--extra BRANCH:PATH` files read with `git show`.
- Public = name does not start with an underscore (dunder names count as private). Nested functions are not listed.
- Module docstring: `ast.get_docstring(module)` is not None. Function/class docstring: same on the node.
- Parameter mention: whole-word occurrence of the parameter name in the function's own docstring (`self`/`cls` excluded; `*args`/`**kwargs` matched by their bare name).
- Third-party libraries: numpy, pandas, scipy, sklearn, joblib, yaml, matplotlib, pyarrow. Imports inside functions count. First-party calls (nbr, ml_group9) and bare-name calls (builtins, local functions) are not listed; standard-library modules (sys.stdlib_module_names) are counted in section 7.
- Resolution: level A through import aliases; level B through annotations (`x: pd.DataFrame`) and assignments from level-A expressions (`m = sparse.csr_matrix(...)`, tuple unpacking as `call()[i]`); level C when the receiver was derived by indexing or a method call; everything else level D.
- Control flow is ignored: the last assignment to a name in source order wins inside its scope; a reassignment from an unresolvable value clears the binding.
- Keyword arguments are listed by name only; positional values are not inspected.
